If you do decide to take a crack at this, please do two things:
1) Make sure you have an exit strategy. If this doesn't work for you, make sure you haven't left yourself in a situation where you've lost data/personal files or that you have a device that you can no longer use.
2) Report back! As you'll see from the links (and others that you'll find on your own), you are definitely not alone in wondering about this platform-OS combo. If you find anything - good or bad - you can help back sharing that info.
Now that is some solid advice. Especially the exit strategy.

As mentioned, a live disc would be best to start. It will give you an idea if the interface of a particular distro is to your liking. In your case, I imagine you would need to pick up an inexpensive external drive to do this. I would recommend Lubuntu or LXLE. LXDE is very lean and efficient, without going off into the deep end of unconventional interfaces like Enlightenment or Blackbox. If you do decide you like Englightenment, Bodhi is a good distro. I use Linux a lot in Virtual Box with only 2GB of RAM and one processing core dedicated to the process, so you can definitely find something that will work adequately well on your device.

Also, before you commit to replacing windows fully, create a backup image to an external drive. That way if things ever really go sour, you have a safety net.
